question:
A model with fixed overall aquifer geometry is divided into more vertical layers. Which statements
are correct? (Select ALL correct answers.)
success:
Correct. Increasing vertical resolution subdivides the same aquifer geometry and can represent
vertical head variation. It does not introduce physical time steps into a steady-state calculation.
A partly saturated cell still contains a saturated portion and must be distinguished from a cell
with no saturated thickness.
error:
Not quite. Separate spatial resolution from physical time. Also compare partial saturation with a
fully dry condition: a water table inside a convertible cell leaves part of that cell saturated.

question:
Which statements correctly describe the numerical approaches being compared in this Solver Lab?
(Select ALL correct answers.)
success:
Correct. The nonlinear formulation and the inner linear solver play different roles. This lab
compares MODFLOW-2005 PCG, MODFLOW-NWT with its Newton formulation and GMRES option, and a MODFLOW 6
Picard setup with CG. No method guarantees convergence for every setup, and outer iteration counts
alone do not measure total computational cost.
error:
Not quite. Distinguish the treatment of nonlinear equations from the solution of each linear system.
Also consider the work within an outer iteration and the possibility of failure under difficult
hydraulic or numerical conditions.

question:
When can comparison with an analytical solution provide a useful numerical verification check?
(Select ALL correct answers.)
success:
Correct. Analytical verification requires matching the problem and its assumptions. Homogeneity does
not eliminate vertical gradients or ensure that a reduced one-dimensional expression applies.
Agreement supports numerical verification of that idealized problem; it does not independently
validate a field model.
error:
Not quite. Check more than hydraulic conductivity: compare flow dimensionality, boundary conditions,
geometry, and the assumptions behind the formula. Distinguish verifying a numerical calculation from
validating its representation of a real aquifer.

question:
How should a randomly generated conductivity field be handled when comparing different solver
engines? (Select ALL correct answers.)
success:
Correct. A controlled engine comparison uses the same spatial conductivity field and other model
inputs. Recorded generation settings and exported conductivity arrays support reproducibility.
Comparing the actual arrays confirms that the hydraulic problem is unchanged. Different arrangements
of the same conductivity values can produce different flows and heads.
error:
Not quite. A conductivity field is defined by its spatial arrangement as well as its distribution.
Reuse a frozen realization and verify the actual arrays; matching only the mean or independently
drawing new fields does not isolate an engine effect.

question:
Which statements correctly describe initial heads in a steady-state calculation? (Select ALL correct
answers.)
success:
Correct. Initial heads are numerical starting estimates in this steady-state experiment. They can
affect convergence and drying or wetting transitions, while the CHD boundary heads remain
prescribed. Whether a cell is initially saturated depends on head relative to that cell's
elevations, not simply on whether head is positive.
error:
Not quite. Compare an initial head with the top and bottom of each cell and distinguish it from a
specified boundary head. The numerical starting estimate can influence the path toward a solution
without changing the imposed steady-state stresses.

question:
Which checks are useful when assessing a calculation in which cells may dry? (Select ALL correct
answers.)
success:
Correct. Solver diagnostics, water budgets, saturation states, and physically interpretable heads
provide complementary evidence. A normal program exit does not replace checking convergence. Special
values used to indicate dry or inactive cells must be identified and excluded from ordinary head
calculations.
error:
Not quite. Separate successful program execution from successful numerical solution. Then check the
hydraulic results and cell states. A dry or inactive marker is a status indicator, not a head that
can be averaged or contoured as if it were a physical value.
